intentions: Create a command-line interface (CLI) to allow users to add, view, update, and delete customers and orders.
Define customer and order data models with attributes such as name, email, order ID, items, and status.
Ensure dependency injection between services and repositories to maintain loose coupling and testability.
Implement business rules in the service layer, such as validating order totals, enforcing order status transitions, and ensuring data consistency.
Provide error handling and validation at both the service and input layers to maintain data integrity.
Separate data access logic into repositories for customer and order persistence using a database or file storage.
Structure the application into modular components: models, repositories, services, and CLI, each with a clear responsibility.
